note: Russell Soundex patent (1918) assigned to Remington Typewriter Company; commercialized as SOUNDEX by successor Rand Kardex Bureau (filed 1927). Canonical example of the patent-trademark lineage this project documents.
Odell improvement patent (1922) also assigned to Remington Typewriter Company; both patents underlie the SOUNDEX trademark filed by Rand Kardex Bureau in 1927.
Second SOUNDEX trademark (filed 1927-10-08) covering the advertising slogan used with the Odell-patent system.

Visible Index patent (1939) granted October 31, 1939 — 44 days before Remington Rand filed the KARDEX trademark (December 14, 1939). The patent describes the overlapping-tray visible card mechanism; the trademark registers the product-line name under which that mechanism was sold commercially.

Loose-Leaf Book And Method Of Assembly patent (granted February 24, 1925) assigned to Wilson Jones Loose Leaf Company; first commercial use of the VI-DEX mark recorded June 27, 1925 — four months after the patent issued. Trademark filed July 22, 1927.

Loose-Leaf Binder patent (granted January 11, 1927) assigned to Wilson Jones Co; REDIREF first commercial use recorded January 5, 1927 — essentially simultaneous with the patent grant. Companion mark HANDIREF (71254950) filed the same day, September 19, 1927.

File Folder patent (granted December 3, 1929) assigned to Yawman & Erbe Mfg Co; SHANNON trademark filed January 23, 1930 — 51 days later. SHANNON was an established British arch-binder brand name Yawman & Erbe was registering for the American market.
